m24_b001: Don't look at me like that. I've just been upstairs with the pass Wilde arranged. I came straight down without changing.
Of course it does. It's made to Upper Level standards. The cuff buttons, the height of the collar. Nothing out of place.
I used to have a whole wardrobe of clothes like this. Now there's just this one. I'm careful even sitting down in it.
Yes. Look at the goods first. I'll tell you about it in a moment.
m24_b002: The checkpoint officer spent ages going through my documents. Halfway through, he looked up. 'You're the daughter from the embezzlement case?'
I said my name was Eleanor. It was on the documents.
Then he asked, 'I hear you're working as a pawnbroker's maid down below?'
Someone beside him laughed. Someone who used to come to dinner at our house. I called him Uncle when I was little.
Do you know the funniest part? I wasn't frightened at all.
I stood there thinking about the way you inspect goods. However fine someone's words, you look at the goods. If there's nothing wrong with them, the words don't need an answer.
m24_b003: The contact you arranged submitted my documents the day before. He recorded the name of every person who handled each procedure.
The officer's face changed when he saw those names. He went through the remaining pages very quickly.
'Nobody downstairs wants to mishandle a favor for that pawnbroker.' ...How many favors do you owe down here, and how many are owed to you?
m24_b004: Every procedure was followed properly. Every page stamped. Every expense listed.
He went back and forth, couldn't find a single fault, and finally had to push my papers back.
You said good goods can stand by their price. Turns out documents can too.
m24_b005: In the end he only said, "You may go, Miss Eleanor."
He pushed my papers to the edge of the window and called the next person. I picked them up and walked through.
Only when the gate clicked behind me did I notice how tightly I was clutching the papers.
Write it down. I'm not buying anything from him.
*She can't help a laugh* ...Then keep it.
Very. I never used to think it was that long.
People recognized me. First they asked about Mother, then what I do now. I said I work in the Lower Level. The owner knows goods, and his accounts are cleaner than theirs.
m24_b006: Mother still can't go back. I asked very carefully. Reviewing my pass doesn't revoke her exile.
She says it's enough for me to go and do what I need to. I shouldn't stop my own life waiting for hers.
m24_b007: Mother's case is still under review. When people ask, I only tell them what's confirmed. I haven't promised the rest in advance.
m24_b008: I brought Mother's formal notice too. If anyone asks, I show them. Her innocence has been established. My business is still mine to build.
Keep it safe. One step at a time.
m24_b009: Your name is on the pass. The agreement—
It's my name on the document. But in their mouths, I'm still 'the daughter from that case,' or 'the pawnbroker's maid.'
I said getting back didn't mean a pass. It meant that when they mentioned me, they meant Eleanor.
m24_b010: Master, tell me. Do I look better in this, or the other outfit?
This one's for the people upstairs.
m25_b001: Don't speak yet. Look at this.
m25_b002: She sets a small parcel on the counter and unwraps it. Inside is a cleaned screwdriver, its tip unchipped and its handle secured again. A densely written label lies beside it.
The sample for my first order. A household upstairs is renovating its growing room. They want reliable used equipment and materials.
New is expensive. They don't trust used. People upstairs think nine out of ten things from down here are stolen.
How do you make them trust it?
Origin, condition, repairs, replacements. Everything on the label. I recorded who found each piece and in which scavenging area.
Goods from below, inspection below, buyers above. You need to understand both ends to make it work.
The sample is already paid for. Take it through the usual trade. The other goods are separate; we can discuss those if you want them.
m25_b003: You pick up the screwdriver and turn it over. Check the tip, the handle joint, every detail on her label. She waits across the counter without speaking.
*She breathes in very slowly, then out again.*
I've waited a long time to hear that.
Yes. You're not allowed to tease me.
m25_b004: Before delivery, someone told that household my goods were stolen stock from a pawnshop.
An Upper Level dealer that's been trading in used goods for years. My family used to buy from them.
The household asked me about it. I laid out the origin records for every piece, and went through them page by page.
Finally they asked the dealer: can you produce records like these for your own goods?
I signed the contract. My own name.
m25_b005: The person who introduced me came out of regard for you. He said, 'People upstairs have heard about that pawnbroker's eye too.'
m25_b006: You paid for the training, samples, trial work—all of it. They tested the sample several times before agreeing on a delivery date.
m25_b007: It's all ordinary equipment and existing seeds. Nothing from the research we returned. I did use everything Mother taught me about the basics.
m25_b008: The public research trials asked about procurement too. I inspect and supply goods. I won't write Mother's research down as mine.
m25_b009: The second time I brought goods in, I insisted on naming the price first. You said I had two right and one uncertain, then tried to charge tuition. I remember.
So half this order is yours.
I say half, I mean half. ...Is it that difficult to give me proper credit, Master?
m26_b001: This is the pawnshop? ...Smaller than I expected.
Neither. I've come to discuss business.
There's a new supplier upstairs. Eleanor. Clean goods, complete records, fair prices. Several of us have been asking where she gets her stock.
I'd like to deal directly with you. You supply, I buy. No need for her in the middle.
You're a pawnbroker from downstairs. How much can she be giving you? I'll pay twice as much.
m26_b003: My goods sell at my prices. Her business isn't mine to sell.
Not for ten times as much.
m26_b004: If you want her goods, speak to her. This shop is only one end of her route.
What if she won't lower her price?
m26_b005: *The buyer laughs and slips a business card back into a pocket.*
I went to her first. I said if she wouldn't lower her price, I'd go around her and talk to her people below.
She said, 'Go ahead. He won't go around me.'
It seems I still need her for inspections and delivery dates. With you two working together, at least I know who is responsible.
Today, consider me a customer. Quote your usual prices.
m26_b007: Next time I go up, I will discuss delivery with her. For a large order, we will still have to negotiate the price.
One more thing, boss. When she introduces her supplier, she never says 'some pawnshop downstairs.' She says 'someone I trust.'
m27_b002: It's over. I mean the launch Wilde helped arrange. We held it today.
A lot of people came. More than I expected.
Samples at the front, records beside them. Some people looked at the clothes and jewelry first, then turned back to the records.
Afterward, some stayed asking questions until the end. When could the next batch arrive? Could we sign a long-term contract?
m27_b003: Yes. When the formal notice arrived, she looked at it for ages. She took it out again before leaving today.
She stood in the last row and listened to everything. I got one number wrong and she frowned from the back. ...Just like at the farm.
m27_b004: Mother didn't come. The formal result still hasn't arrived. She says she doesn't want to stand in front of people until the case is settled.
Have you told her about today?
I rehearsed it for her last night. She picked out three things, and people asked about all three today. When the notice arrives, I'll take her to see it.
m27_b005: Mother still can't go upstairs. The night before, she made me rehearse it in our room and found three weak points.
People asked about all three today.
m27_b006: Then someone came to see me. One of the biggest procurement firms upstairs. The person in charge came in person.
The contract was worth more than all my current orders together.
Remove that pawnshop downstairs from the supplier and partner list. People upstairs don't like dealing with pawnshops. And there are unpleasant rumors.
...Just like Lydia at the beginning. Back then it was 'stop mentioning your mother's case.' Today it's 'stop mentioning that pawnshop.'
'Where my goods come from, who inspected them, who provided my first capital: not a single name comes off that list. If you object to a pawnshop, find someone else.'
Then someone at the back came forward and said they'd sign. A little later, a second person did too.
When that manager left, his face looked worse than mine after my first Nutrifruit.
m27_b007: Half the people came through your connections. Someone told me they were there to show support for that shopkeeper.
I told them I didn't need a cheering section. Since they'd come, they should look at the goods.
m27_b008: Someone asked whether the supply was reliable. I said half the scavengers and owners downstairs knew my mas... my business partner.
You didn't hear that. I corrected it.
...Then pretend you didn't. Lydia was the only person there who laughed.
m27_b009: The venue, the samples, the arrangements. You spared none of it. Nobody could claim this presentation only succeeded through someone else's influence.
m27_b010: Lydia was there too. Afterward she came running over, but the first thing she said wasn't praise.
'They kept calling you by your name.'
Only then did I realize. Not once all day did anyone call me 'the daughter from that case.'
m27_b011: Next time, I will. I set the terms. I should be the one to say when they're fulfilled.
Today I need to go home and change first.
m28_b002: She pauses in the doorway, checks that there are no other customers, then approaches the counter.
There is something to settle today. Afterwards, I want to spend a little longer here.
I have kept the rest of the day for you.
Until the day you return to the upper district under your own name.
That day has come. They remember my name, and trust me with their business.
You kept your promise, and I have done the work I promised. Our original agreement ends today.
I know. I will miss having someone tell me off every day.
Someone upstairs invited me to dinner to discuss next season. I asked him to arrange another time.
Because you had plans with me?
What else? ...And you cannot count this outfit as work today.
What should I count it as?
Coming to see you. I used to want to stay after the work was done. Now I have a business of my own, and I still want to come.
...Must I say what I call you as well?
m28_b003: She comes to your side and places her hand in yours. You hold it, reluctant to let go.
The old agreement has ended. That name has not. Did you hear me?
m28_b005: Then let's make a new agreement. No end date this time.
First, don't use that name to tease me in front of customers. That hasn't changed.
Second, you don't decide my business upstairs for me. Your business downstairs, I will fuss over, until you're sick of it.
We make them together. I'm not unreasonable.
Third, eat every day. I'll check.
No end date. ...You said it yourself.
m28_b006: I hear you. Come here, my lady.
...Never mind. A little closer is possible.
m28_b007: Since it's your choice, I'll take that 'master' to heart.
m28_b008: She pauses, as if deliberately making you wait.
This time, I decided. Nobody can change that. Not even you.
m28_b010: She leans into your arms, her skirt brushing the counter. She paid to have this outfit made from an old dress. The first time she wore it here, she hadn't known where to put her hands, hadn't finished the curtsy. Now she can afford far finer clothes, and still chooses this set to see you.
People say I'm harder to get hold of than I used to be.
m28_b011:
The first time she entered this pawnshop, she said it barely counted as a shop, and hardly wanted to touch the counter.
Later, she learned to identify goods, keep accounts, and wipe that counter. She left the pen beside your usual hand, set replaced casings apart, and looked back from the door again and again to say, 'See you tomorrow, Master.'
Now the Upper Level remembers her name again. People wait for her answers, invite her to examine samples, entrust her with proper business. When they mention that pawnbroker downstairs, she never lets 'he happened to help a little' pass as an account of what you did.
You haven't moved upstairs. The pawnshop opens as usual. There is still a familiar place for her beside the counter.
Sometimes she returns with formal business. Sometimes she changes into that outfit and waits for the last customer to leave before coming to your side.
She can walk through those doors that once shut against her on her own. And she knows whose presence she chooses to bow her head in, before looking up again and saying, 'Master.'
